new_sources.title: United Kingdom — Financial Services Act 2012, chapter 21, as enacted
new_sources.jurisdiction: United Kingdom; section 121 specifies England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
new_sources.legal_status: Enacted primary legislation, deliberately used as historical text. Assent is not assumed to commence every provision; no current consolidated-law claim.
new_sources.actual_inspection: Official 385-page PDF retrieved; read assent page (printed1), section6 insertion of FSMA1B–1E (printed20–22), 2B and2G (printed29/31), 3B (printed34–35), and sections121–122 (printed210). No whole-Act review claimed.
new_sources.supports: Distinct consumer/integrity/competition and prudential safety/soundness objectives; no requirement to prevent every firm failure; resource efficiency, proportionality and transparency principles.
new_sources.limits: Not a capital ratio, automatic resolution power, enforcement outcome or welfare optimum. Section122 leaves remaining commencement to Treasury orders, not inspected here. Later amendments and institutional changes are outside this historical snapshot.

new_sources.title: Financial Stability Board — Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions, revised version2024
new_sources.jurisdiction: International standard; domestic implementation and authority remain separate.
new_sources.legal_status: FSB resolution standard with implementation guidance. The foreword distinguishes the twelve Key Attributes from their annex guidance; neither supplies a particular national statutory power.
new_sources.actual_inspection: Actual94-page PDF: foreword printed1–2; preamble4–5; KA1.1 and2.1–2.5, printed6–7; KA3.5–3.6, printed10; KA5.1–5.2, printed12; KA6.1–6.5, printed13. Publication page confirms the2024 revision concerns FMI annex guidance.
new_sources.supports: Continuity and orderly exit; bail-in loss allocation/conversion; creditor hierarchy and liquidation-comparator compensation; temporary resolution funding with explicit conditions and loss recovery; authority independence/accountability.
new_sources.limits: No promise that recapitalisation creates cash, every creditor is protected, public liquidity is never used, or a national authority has these powers. Annexes, CCP calibration and country implementation are not comprehensively reviewed.

authoring_boundaries: Describe the UK case as what the2012 enacted text specified, not as an exhaustive account of present law. Do not import uninspected commencement dates, amendments or current statutory thresholds.

Resolution bookkeeping must separately fund any continued payments and identify who absorbs losses. A liability conversion can change capital without adding cash; a hierarchy or compensation mechanism requires an explicitly stipulated comparator and source of funds.

Explain boundary arbitrage and regulatory capture with a transparent original incentive mechanism, preserving the distinction between a possible mechanism and empirical proof about a regulator. Consultation or an unfavorable rule alone is not evidence of capture.
